parameters.polygon: regular convex 120-gon, vertices in counterclockwise cyclic order
parameters.construction: straight-line triangulation using polygon vertices only
parameters.objective: minimize over triangulations the maximum, over distinct vertex pairs, of shortest-path length divided by Euclidean chord length

best_human.provenance: The published 6-fan rule was rebuilt for n=120. The full edge set was checked, and its dilation was recomputed with rational interval bounds.
best_human.ai_provenance: Classical human construction; no AI provenance stated by the source.
best_human.evidence_state: same-parameter witness and certified score reproduced; score is the interval upper endpoint rounded upward

best_public.source_location: Theorem: dilation of vertices of any regular polygon is less than 1.4482
best_public.provenance: Published universal upper bound on the optimum. The theorem's specific n=120 triangulation is not reconstructed here.
best_public.evidence_state: reported theorem bound; witness not locally reproduced

best_reproduced.provenance: Task-local rebuild of the UBC 6-fan rule; certified with rational chord and path intervals.
best_reproduced.ai_provenance: Benchmark reconstruction of a published human method.
best_reproduced.evidence_state: valid triangulation; objective enclosed by the interval in sota.json

frozen_human_baseline.provenance: Rebuilt UBC 6-fan construction; upward-rounded certified upper endpoint.

highest_reported.metric: maximum shortest-path length divided by Euclidean chord length
highest_reported.reproduction_status: theorem bound reported; the specific 120-gon witness was not reconstructed
